audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart reads [Skill, Malzahar, Malzahar, Skill, Malzahar, Skill, Aurelion Sol]; the packet and content layer both read [Malzahar, Skill, Skill, Malzahar, Malzahar, Malzahar, Skill]. Six rows disagree.
audit.why: Malzahar's ranged harass beats the walk-up Q stacking level 1; 2-3 settle even; 4-5 and item one the permanent shove denies the Stardust economy; fully stacked late it evens back out. 50.15% WR over 1370 games fits a tempo-vs-scaling coinflip.
audit.corrected: All six disagreeing full-layer sides moved to match win[], ratings and whys rewritten with them.

audit.why: Spikes are grounded and complete: shove out-tempos his stacking 3-5, level 6 Grasp cancels his setup, first-item pin, late Stardust range evens it. All four spikes[] present.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three flagged missing interactions absent: Singularity's execute threshold, Astral Flight running down a dashless Malzahar's retreat, and Singularity bypassing stacked resistances. breakdown.cooldowns has no digit; dos/donts carry pasted tradeGood/tradeBad; tradeGood references poking 'his shield off' — Aurelion Sol has no shield.
audit.why: Astral Flight is 22s rank 1 / 16s max and is his only reposition — the punish window. Singularity is 12s with a center execute. His Q and W are channels, so your Q silence interrupts both. Your R channel can be cancelled by his R stun — Falling Star is 120/110/100s.
audit.corrected: See edits: real cooldowns, execute and flight-chase written into dontsFull and cooldowns, trade strings rebuilt on his actual kit.

edits.before: Aurelion Sol wins by landing Astral Flight, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol wins by stacking Stardust in peace, dragging you into Singularity's execute, and out-ranging you late.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Silence-and-punish: his Q and W are channels, so a Q silence cuts the breath mid-trade — land E-Q-W while Astral Flight is on its 22-second cooldown.

edits.before: E a caster minion and let the visions farm for you — your lane is a macro pattern, not a duel, from the first wave.
edits.after: Your ranged E-W harass beats his walk-up Q stacking level 1 — bill him for every breath he channels on the wave.

edits.before: Q online: the silence is your trade answer. Use it on his engage spell, not on poke he can walk around.
edits.after: Even now: he farms and stacks safely — hold your Q silence for his Astral Flight step-up, not stray breath poke.

edits.before: W voidlings turn your shove permanent — the wave hits his tower while you ward, roam-shadow, or just exist safely.
edits.after: Still even: neither converts a kill threat yet — keep the voidling shove rolling and start counting his stacks.

edits.before: Lost Chapter and the machine is complete: E-hops fund themselves, the wave is always crashing, and his tower is always bleeding.
edits.after: Lost Chapter completes the machine: your permanent crash denies the free Q-stacking economy his whole kit scales on.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: visions melt waves AND health bars. Suppress-into-burn kills through most defensive answers.
edits.after: Liandry's spike: the pin under tower keeps him off tempo — his stacks stall while your burn melts wave and bar.

edits.before: Late Malz is a number: one suppression on their carry equals one won teamfight. Shield up, flank smart, press R.
edits.after: Fully stacked, his expanded ult and Q out-range you — the late game is even, decided by who lands R first.

edits.before: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight: matchup-defining — His reposition and escape — he is a stationary battery while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - spell shield (Iron Boundary) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight (W): 22s at rank 1, 16s maxed — his only reposition; he is a stationary battery while it is down. - Singularity (E) is 12s: sidestep the pull and its center execute never threatens. - Your R is 140/110/80s — spend it on fights, not waves.

edits.before: Good trade: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets. Bad trade: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: Good trade: Silence-and-punish — his Q and W are channels, so a Q silence cuts the breath mid-trade; land E-Q-W while Astral Flight sits on its 22-second cooldown. Bad trade: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: His whole kit scales on Stardust farmed in peace — a wave that is always crashing forces him to choose between CS and ever stacking on you.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: At half shield you lose the exchange: Singularity drags you toward its execute center and Astral Flight runs down a Malzahar with no dash.

edits.before: Flash + Teleport standard — TP doubles your shove-tax map game. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport standard — TP turns every crash into cross-map pressure. Ghost-cleanse setups exist into hard dive; Ignite pairs with R kill threats if you want lane blood.
